newsitem.title: USA: Continental mulling exclusive Boeing pact.
newsitem.headline: Continental mulling exclusive Boeing pact.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc., which is in negotiations on a wide-body jet order, said Monday it has asked Boeing Co. to provide details about a possible exclusive deal for planes.
Continental said it is currently negotiating with two manufacturers for the jet order.

As part of those talks, Continental asked Boeing to submit additional details about possibly forging an exclusive supplier relationship, said Continental spokeswoman Karla Villalon. Continental declined to comment further.
Boeing has recently forged exclusive provider relationships with American Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc.
European consortium Airbus Industrie called sole-supplier deals as "bad for business."
"We have never engaged in exclusive deals," said Airbus spokesman David Venz. "They asked Boeing, in light of the last two deals.
"We think it's bad for business," he said. "Airlines that go into that have to be aware of the apparent short-term gain in terms of long-term pain," Venz said.

Airbus said Boeing has aggressively pursued exclusive contracts with some of its existing, major customers. Boeing negotiated for future aircraft orders, while also offering to renegotiate past contracts, Venz said.

Last month Continental said it was in talks with both Boeing and Airbus about buying up to 40 long-range passenger jets. The aircraft would replace McDonnell Douglas Corp. DC-10 jets that Continental wants to retire from its fleet.
At that time, Continental said it would make a decision within two months about the 40-jet deal, which the airline valued at about $1.8 billion to $2.8 billion.
